notes.record: THE load-bearing phase. Root cause of the star: relations are refines (134) + derives_from (85), BOTH hierarchical. A parent-pointer vocabulary can only ever produce a tree -- log2(N) degree is unreachable without lateral relations. Must precede phases 5-7, or added edges just fatten the same hubs.

notes.record: Two things this changes: (1) jaxfne's .lab graph already has 9 depends_on edges (see lab_balance.py RELATIONS output) that repo_mapper.py does not emit -- these are hand-added and survive re-scan per repo_mapper.md's 'links added by hand also survive a re-scan' contract, but there is no grammar/closed-set validation on the .lab/ side (unlike server/tools.py's _VALID_RELATIONS, which governs a separate live MCP claim-graph, not .lab/ JSON files) -- so this is informal, undocumented drift, not an accepted vocabulary extension. (2) DESIGN.md names supports/contradicts/questions as real edge-template relations, but only for the live claim graph's claim_links table, which the docs explicitly say has reasoning/confidence fields (title/action/transformation/context/confidence/fitness) that .lab/'s links[] does not carry at all. None of tested_by/documents/implements/constrains/supersedes/co_evolves_with (5 of the original 8 proposed here) appear anywhere in either doc -- phase 4 is a genuinely new proposal to send upstream, not adoption of an existing labyrinth spec.

issues.title: The star topology is produced by repo_mapper itself -- labyrinth's own graph has it worse
issues.detail: Ran scripts/lab_balance.py against labyrinth's OWN artifacts/.lab (106 nodes): Gini 0.530, max degree 75 (labyrinth-plan), degree variance 80.6, 91/106 nodes never referenced, and a depth histogram of {0:1, 1:14, 2:91} -- no depth-3 tier exists at all. jaxfne's numbers are Gini 0.539, max 71, variance 53.4. Labyrinth's graph is by some measures MORE star-shaped than the repo it maps.
issues.implication: The 10-phase rebalance plan is not jaxfne remediation -- it is a protocol-level gap. Any repo repo_mapper touches inherits this shape, because the mapper only ever emits the two hierarchical relations (refines/derives_from) and a parent-pointer vocabulary cannot express anything but a tree. Phase 4 (lateral relation vocabulary) is therefore an upstream feature request, not a local workaround.
issues.next_action: Report to labyrinth: the fix belongs in the mapper's relation vocabulary, so every adopting repo benefits.

issues.title: repo_mapper's own degree-variance metric exempts hubs, making it blind to the star it creates
issues.detail: On the same labyrinth graph, repo_mapper self-reports 'degree variance 1.08 (n=96, 11 hub-exempt)' while scripts/lab_balance.py measures 80.6 over all 106 nodes. The gap is entirely the hub exemption: excluding the 11 highest-degree nodes removes precisely the evidence of a star. Same pattern on jaxfne -- mapper says 2.96 (21 hub-exempt), harness says 53.4.
issues.risk: A graph can report near-perfect convergence (1.08, Fano 0.49) while containing a degree-75 hub and 91 never-referenced nodes. Any agent trusting the mapper's own health number would conclude this graph is fine. It is the metric, not the graph, that is passing.
issues.next_action: Report upstream: publish the unexempted variance/Gini alongside the exempted figure, or at minimum print the exempted node count AND their degrees so the exemption is visible rather than silent.

issues.title: Draft proposal: extend .lab/ (repo_mapper.py) relation vocabulary from 2 to a documented, grammar-checked set
issues.detail: Scoped to the .lab/ JSON side only -- explicitly NOT proposing changes to server/tools.py's separate _VALID_RELATIONS (that governs the live MCP claim-graph, a different data store with its own reasoning/confidence edge fields .lab/ does not have). Proposed set, in three tiers: (a) already informally in use -- depends_on (9 real edges in jaxfne's graph today, currently unvalidated); (b) already named in DESIGN.md for the sibling live-graph vocabulary, reusable as-is since the semantics transfer -- supports, contradicts, questions; (c) new, not in either doc, needed for a code-repo graph specifically -- tested_by, documents, implements, supersedes. Dropped from the original 8: constrains and co_evolves_with -- too semantically close to depends_on/supports respectively to justify as distinct grammar-checked relations without a concrete jaxfne use case demonstrating the difference; can be reconsidered if a real need surfaces.
issues.implication: find_violations() in server/objective_grammar.py checks node-id lineage against real links but (per the verbatim docs) has no relation-vocabulary check at all today -- so this proposal's second half, alongside the vocabulary itself, is that analyze() gain a closed-set check for .lab/ relation strings (mirroring _VALID_RELATIONS' role on the live-graph side), so an unrecognized relation string surfaces as a grammar violation instead of silently surviving re-scans the way depends_on has been.
issues.next_action: This is a draft for human review before anything is sent upstream to the labyrinth maintainers -- not committed as accepted, per Reflexivity of Amendment (protocol-tier changes need explicit human approval, not agent self-confirmation).
